document.title: Commander's Initial Assessment
document.authors: Headquarters, International Security Assistance Force, Kabul (Gen. Stanley McChrystal)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan 20/20: The 20-Year War in 20 Documents | National Security Archive
document.note: [Confidential] Key document behind Obama's 2009 surge. McChrystal calls for a properly resourced counterinsurgency campaign with 40,000-60,000 more troops. It leaked to the Washington Post and was declassified by DoD in Sept 2009. It assumes the Taliban sanctuaries in Pakistan would not sustain the insurgency indefinitely.

events.description: President Obama speech outlining new US Strategy for Afghanistan and Pakistan.
Secretary of Defense directed CENTCOM to provide a multidisciplinary assessment of Afghanistan.
SACEUR and NATO Secretary General issued a similar directive for an assessment.
CENTCOM directed COMISAF/USFOR-A to complete the overall review.
McChrystal submitted the Initial Assessment to Secretary Gates from Kabul.
Publication of the Commander's Initial Assessment describing the insurgency (QST, HQN, HiG) and external influences
Target for ANA to reach 134,000 strength by Fall 2010, with a ceiling of 240,000.
The recent Presidential and Provincial Council elections were executed smoothly from a security standpoint, but their credibility remains an open question.
Afghan Presidential and Provincial Council elections, with a spike of insurgent violence (3-4 times average attacks) against ISAF and ANSF, mainly in the south and east.
Efforts to formalize ISAF-ANSF partnership begin.
Framework and FRAGO issued directing ISAF-ANSF partnering.
NATO North Atlantic Council approved creation of an intermediate three-star command (ISAF Joint Command) between COMISAF and the RCs.
Eikenberry and McChrystal signed the USG Integrated Civil-Military Campaign Plan, forwarded to Holbrooke and Petraeus.
Planned initial operational capability of NTM-A.
Planned IOC of ISAF Joint Command (FOC 12 Nov 2009).
ISAF established the CIVCAS Tracking Cell.
ISAF issued a revised Tactical Directive to all troops, describing how and when lethal force should be used and stressing civilian protection.
Military Technical Agreement between ISAF and GIRoA; ISAF not required to pay compensation for damage to civilian or governmental property.
Decision to grow the ANP by 4.8K to provide security for Kabul ahead of the Afghan national elections.
North Atlantic Council endorsed creation of NATO Training Mission-Afghanistan (NTM-A).
NTM-A scheduled to stand up in mid-September to generate forces and provide institutional training.
Planned start of accelerated ANA growth.
Serena Hotel bombing, cited as an example of lethal operations planned from the prison system.
Decision made to grow ANP by 4.8K to provide security for Kabul ahead of national elections; followed by a further 10K growth for 14 key provinces.
NTM-A scheduled to stand up in mid-September 2009.
NATO's North Atlantic Council approved creation of an intermediate three-star command (ISAF Joint Command) between COMISAF and the RCs.
Planned Initial Operational Capability of the ISAF Joint Command.
Planned Full Operational Capability of the ISAF Joint Command.
Planned Initial Operational Capability of NATO Training Mission-Afghanistan.
HQ ISAF issued FRAGO 408-2009 directing establishment of a National Military Coordination Center with GIRoA.
actors: Government of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan

events.description: Commander's Initial Assessment concludes that ISAF needs a new, properly resourced population-centric strategy and more forces.
A multidisciplinary Joint Operational Planning Group is formed to assess the ISAF counterinsurgency campaign strategy, OPLAN and OPORD as part of the Initial Assessment.
Efforts began to formalize ISAF–ANSF partnership.
Framework developed and FRAGO issued directing ISAF–ANSF partnering.
Joint Operational Planning Group formed to assess ISAF campaign strategy as part of the Initial Assessment.
CSTC-A transitioning to NATO Training Mission-Afghanistan concurrently with formation of ISAF Joint Command.
Military Technical Agreement between ISAF and GIRoA, under which ISAF is not required to compensate for civilian or governmental property damage.
actors: Government of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan

events.description: USFOR-A proposes forming a new Combined Joint Interagency Task Force for detention and rule of law operations.
Eikenberry and McChrystal sign the Integrated Civil-Military Campaign Plan and forward it to Holbrooke and Petraeus.
Revised Tactical Directive on protection of civilians issued, cited as a key StratCom tool.
Bonn Agreement on provisional arrangements in Afghanistan signed.
actors: Government of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan

events.description: Military Technical Agreement between ISAF and the Interim Administration of Afghanistan.
UNSCR 1386 authorized deployment of ISAF for six months.
UNSCR 1401 established UNAMA.
UNSCR 1510 authorized ISAF expansion beyond Kabul.
Bucharest Summit Declaration.
COMISAF Commander's Initial Guidance issued.
COMISAF Tactical Directive issued.
QST establishes a body to receive complaints against its own officials and ombudsmen to investigate abuse of power, plus shari'a courts.
OXFAM report indicating significant diversion of development funding is cited.
Planned second stage (strategic consolidation) as ISAF and ANSF capabilities grow over the next 12-24 months.
A revised Tactical Directive on the use of lethal force was issued to all troops in theatre.
The Military Technical Agreement between ISAF and GIRoA was dated 4 Jan 2002.
actors: Government of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan

events.description: Quetta Shura conducts formal annual winter campaign review; Mullah Omar then announces guidance for the coming year.
Secretary of Defense directs CENTCOM commander to provide a multidisciplinary assessment of the situation in Afghanistan.
SACEUR and NATO Secretary General issue a similar directive for an assessment.
COMISAF/USFOR-A receives direction from CDRUSCENTCOM to complete the overall review.
McChrystal submits the Initial Assessment to Secretary Gates.
ISAF completed a full review of detainee policies and practices with recommendations for substantial revisions.
Recent Presidential and Provincial Council elections were executed smoothly from a security standpoint, though credibility of results remained in question.
Target: ANA to reach 134,000 strength by Fall 2010, with ceiling of 240,000; ANP target raised to 160,000.
Proposed establishment of an intermediate operational headquarters to improve unity of command and effort.
President Obama gave a speech outlining the new U.S. Strategy for Afghanistan and Pakistan.
McChrystal held consultations with Afghan Defense Minister Wardak during the assessment.
Afghan Presidential and Provincial Council elections; spike in insurgent attacks against ISAF and ANSF at three to four times the average.
ISAF completed a full review of detainee policies and practices, recommending transfer of long-term detention to GIRoA.
Decision to grow the ANP by 4.8K to provide security for Kabul ahead of national elections.
North Atlantic Council endorsed creation of NATO Training Mission-Afghanistan.
NTM-A scheduled to stand up in mid-September.
New CSTC-A-managed police training contract is to begin, replacing INL contracted trainers.

key_claims: McChrystal assesses the overall situation in Afghanistan as serious and deteriorating, though the mission is achievable.
He argues ISAF needs a fundamentally new population-centric counterinsurgency strategy, not just more resources.
He frames the conflict as three regional insurgencies intersecting with local power struggles.
He judges the next 12 months decisive for gaining the initiative before defeating the insurgency becomes impossible.
He warns that Afghan government collapse to the Taliban could again make Afghanistan a base for transnational terrorism, including al-Qaeda.
He says civilian casualties and ISAF's distance from the population risk strategic defeat.
The insurgency is a set of related insurgent groups, principally the Quetta Shura Taliban, the Haqqani Network and Hezb-e Islami Gulbuddin, that coordinate loosely without a formal command structure.
Most insurgent fighters are Afghan, directed by a small number of senior Afghan leaders based in Pakistan.
The QST focuses on Kandahar and runs a shadow government; HQN seeks Khowst, Paktia and Paktika; HiG has bases in Nangarhar, Nuristan and Kunar.
HQN draws resources principally from Pakistan, Gulf Arab networks and its association with al Qaeda.
Al Qaeda's links with HQN have grown, and expanded HQN control could let AQAM re-establish safe havens in Afghanistan.
Some elements of Pakistan's ISI are reportedly aiding the senior leaders of the major Afghan insurgent groups.
Narcotics funding is only one of several insurgent income sources; eliminating it would not end insurgent capability.
There are no clear lines between insurgents, criminal networks and corrupt GIRoA officials.
The Afghan insurgency is clearly supported from Pakistan, and senior leaders of the major insurgent groups are based there.
Some elements of Pakistan's ISI are reportedly aiding the insurgent leadership.
Al Qaeda's links with the Haqqani Network have grown, and expanded HQN control could let AQAM re-establish safe havens in Afghanistan.
Iran's Qods Force is reportedly training fighters for certain Taliban groups, while Iran also supports GIRoA.
Despite Pakistani support, the insurgency in Afghanistan is predominantly Afghan.
Increasing Indian influence in Afghanistan is likely to encourage Pakistani countermeasures.
ISAF should shift to an Afghan-run detention system with intelligence collection and counter-radicalization to avoid 'catch and release'.
Insurgents targeted ISAF and ANSF rather than voters during the elections, despite a spike in violence.
The narco/illicit economy and extortion on development projects undermine governance and GIRoA revenue.
The strategy has three stages: gain the initiative, strategic consolidation (12-24 months), and sustained security.
ISAF must prioritize resources on threatened, high-population areas and requires more forces.
External actors such as Pakistan and Iran are named as risks outside ISAF's control.
Substantial intelligence points directly at the Afghan narcotics industry as a significant economic enabler for the insurgency.
The ISAF OPORD lacks prioritization and does not link the Regional Commands under a single nationwide strategy.
Insurgents traditionally use winter months to reorganize for the fighting season, and ISAF has inadvertently matched this cycle.
Pakistani military operations in the border area are an external event that influences the insurgent operational cycle.
Insurgents have used the information environment effectively to undermine ISAF and GIRoA credibility.
Creation of ISAF Joint Command and NTM-A is intended to improve unity of command.
Insurgents have undermined the credibility of ISAF, the international community and GIRoA through effective information operations, though without gaining credibility themselves.
The operational centre of gravity is the support of the Afghan population; the NATO strategic centre of gravity is Alliance cohesion.
StratCom should be embedded in all operations rather than treated as a separate line of operation.

Offensive IO should expose insurgents' violations, their responsibility for most civilian casualties, and their attacks on education and development, while offering reintegration opportunities for lower-level insurgents.
Civilian casualties undermine support for GIRoA and ISAF, and the Afghan people hold ISAF to a higher standard than the insurgents.
About 14% of people killed and 22% of those wounded in the last recorded six months were hurt during escalation-of-force incidents.
ISAF should be 'first with the known truth' after a civilian casualty incident and should seek ways to reach insurgents in Pakistan.
Taliban and Al Qaeda insurgents make up over 2,500 of 14,500 inmates in the Afghan Corrections System and radicalize other inmates.
Multiple Afghan national prison facilities are described as firmly under Taliban control.
Insurgents use the prison system as a sanctuary and base to plan lethal operations, e.g. the Serena Hotel bombing.
The assessment proposes a Combined Joint Interagency Task Force to run US detention and reform Afghan corrections, with the aim of handing detention over to the Afghan government.
ISAF should be 'first with the known truth' on civilian casualty incidents, because insurgent information operations are not hampered by truthfulness.
The assessment recommends growing the ANA to 134k by Oct 2010 and an estimated 240k, and the ANP to 160k.
The assessment recommends growing the ANP to 160k and the ANSF to a 400k target (240K ANA, 160K ANP).
ANP growth includes doubling district and provincial strength and absorbing the APPF.
NTM-A, endorsed 12 June 2009, would be dual-hatted with CSTC-A, with IJC taking over development of the fielded ANSF.
All police training authority should shift from State's INL to CSTC-A/NTM-A.
CSTC-A should receive direct authority over ASFF, bypassing DSCA and USASAC fees.
